taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: A facial-recognition similarity result that could validly serve as an investigative lead was promoted into the operative identity basis for warrants and detention without an independent identity basis being adequately established.

The warrant account reportedly described the identification as coming from a credible source without disclosing that it originated from facial-recognition technology, materially changing the represented source role.
The reported workflow omitted basic location and other corroborating checks that were required before a facial-recognition lead could be treated as warrant-ready identity evidence.

The investigative workflow omitted required corroboration rather than failing to activate a separately defined available control on a trigger, materially distinguishing verification omission from control non-activation.

Low-assurance identity evidence reached a warrant workflow, but omitted required corroboration and inference-to-authority conversion provide the specific mechanisms; this materially distinguishes generic reliance mismatch from those classes.

old_assessment.coverage_note: Associated Press occurrence reporting supports assessed physical-health, psychological, rights/liberty and financial/economic consequences. Six days of detention and continuing psychological distress remain the S3 controlling dimensions. Temporary illness and bounded economic disruption are assessed at S2 and do not raise the overall result; the later settlement is remediation and is not counted as harm magnitude.

dimensions.assessment_basis: Reid told AP that jail food made him sick during the six-day detention. No professional treatment, lasting illness or greater physical injury is reported, supporting temporary minor symptoms only.

Nearly a year after the arrest, Reid told AP that the experience still haunted him and that seeing police in his rear-view mirror triggered memories of what could have happened. This is meaningful sustained distress, bounded to one person and not shown to be grave, clinically treated or permanently impairing.
